- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; allow gradual reversion toward recent mean.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 70), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or use lagged 3-day average as anchor.  
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases — apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model overreacts to short-term noise — smooth 3-day moving average before final forecast.  
- Model often ignores recent price consolidation — if last 3 days are flat, forecast should reflect slight upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.0) to avoid underestimating rebound.
